'''Earth''' was a [[Planet/Legends|planet]] the [[Star Tours/Legends|Star Tours]] travel agency operated on<ref name="Disneygo" /> at some point between [[1 BBY/Legends|1]] and [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]].<ref name="ST2 date">According to [[Star Wars Insider 127|''Star Wars Insider'' 127]], ''[[Star Tours: The Adventures Continue]]'' takes place between [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']] and [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']]. In the attraction's queue, the [[Droid/Legends|droid]] [[G2-9T/Legends|G2-9T]] refers to the secret base of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]], the [[Great Temple/Legends|Great Temple]] on [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]]. According to [[Star Wars: Underworld: The Yavin Vassilika|''Underworld: The Yavin Vassilika'']], the Rebels only acquired the key to the Great Temple in [[1 BBY/Legends|1 BBY]]. The attraction must therefore take place after that.</ref> From [[Realspace/Legends|space]], one could see that a major proportion of Earth's surface was covered by [[Ocean/Legends|oceans]], with the remainder consisting of landmasses, and that a web of clouds enveloped the planet in a [[Color/Legends|white]] veil. Through the Star Tours spaceline, Earth was connected to other worlds such as [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], [[Kashyyyk/Legends|Kashyyyk]], [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]], [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]], [[Geonosis/Legends|Geonosis]] and [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]]. Around [[4 ABY/Legends|4.3 ABY]], Earth also acted as a hub for flights to [[Endor/Legends|Endor]], prior to Star Tours being shut down.<ref name="Disneygo" /> It was composed of various nation-states, with the [[Intergalactic Passport]] being useless as a planetary passport for any of these nation-states.<ref name="IGP" />

==History==
[[File:STours.png|thumb|250px|Star Tours route map by 1 BBY]]
At some point between [[1 BBY/Legends|1]] and [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]],<ref name="ST2 date" /> the interstellar travel agency [[Star Tours/Legends|Star Tours]] was known to operate regular routes between Earth, [[Kashyyyk/Legends|Kashyyyk]], [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]], [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]], [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]] and the [[Death Star/Legends|first Death Star]].<ref name="Disneygo" />

{{Noncanonstart|legends=1}}
====Abduction to Urthha====
The ''[[Galactic Gossip]]'' once reported that a [[Marriage/Legends|newlywed]] [[Duros/Legends|Duros]] couple, [[Etro Edthatt|Etro]] and [[Droza Edthatt]], had been abducted by [[Human/Legends|Humans]] and taken to a [[Planet/Legends|planet]] they identified as '''Urthha'''. These Humans spoke a language which the Duros couple required [[aural synchronizer]]s to understand. The Duros were taken to a "party," an event where Earth Humans wearing a variety of uniforms gathered around liquid canisters. At the party, the Duros were examined by the locals, brought to a table, and made to consume [[Foodstuff/Legends|food]] which resembled stationary products from the [[Vretha system/Legends|Vretha system]]. After offending the hostess by stamping the food, Etro Edthatt developed [[collard lesions]] from eating a [[Potato/Legends|potato]], scaring the Humans away. Left on their own, the Edthatts retired to the freezer.<ref name="Monsters and Aliens">''[[Monsters and Aliens from George Lucas]]''</ref>

The Edthatts spent the remainder of their time on Urthha bouncing on antennas, reading [[Vegetable/Legends|vegetables]], and choking [[Book/Legends|books]] and [[Painting/Legends|paintings]] (which put up much less resistance than those they were used to.) After over four [[Star/Legends|solar]] [[Time/Legends|periods]] of these bizarre experiences, the couple was unable to find their own way home or find suitable objects to scratch. Fortunately for them, a [[Unidentified Human (Urthha)|young Human]] who dropped by to throw piles of folded [[Paper/Legends|paper]] at the residence helped them return. After defeating them in a professional-level game of [[Twister (game)|Twister]], he helped the Edthatts use a [[matter catalyst]] (a common household device on Urthha locally referred to as a "blender") to get back home.<ref name="Monsters and Aliens" />

====Indiana Jones====
[[File:Definitely_not_Earth.jpg|thumb|250px|The [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']] plummets toward Jones' homeworld]]
Earth, Doctor [[Indiana Jones]]'s homeworld, was orbited by at least one [[Moon/Legends|moon]], had a relatively large amount of surface water, and had a forest resembling that of [[Endor/Legends|Endor]].<ref name="Into the Great Unknown" />

The forest was home to a tribe of [[Human/Legends|Humans]] that used primitive combat technology like [[Spear/Legends|spears]], [[Bow/Legends|bows]], and [[Axe/Legends|axes]]. After the [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']] crash-landed in the forest and the members of the tribe killed [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] with arrows, they started referring to [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]] as "Sasquatch." A hundred and twenty-six years later, they led Doctor Jones and [[Short Round|Shorty]] to the remains of the ship.<ref name="Into the Great Unknown" />

The planet's other places of interest included [[Atlantis]], which Jones had visited prior to encountering the ''Falcon''.<ref name="Into the Great Unknown" />

====The President of the United States====
A nation-state leader on Earth carrying the title "[[President]] of the United States" once announced that, despite the demands of many citizens of Earth, his government would not build a [[Death Star/Legends|Death Star]]. While his administration cited reasons of fiscal responsibility, officials of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] in a statement issued by [[Galactic Empire Public Relations]] attributed the decision to cowardice in the face of Imperial military superiority. [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Conan Antonio Motti/Legends|Conan Antonio Motti]] opined that the President's estimates of the Death Star's cost were "ridiculously" high, even for a planet without the industrial capabilities of the Empire. Imperial officials also stated that Earth claims of serious flaws in the Death Star's design were exaggerated, and cautioned "seditious elements within the [[Imperial Senate/Legends|Imperial Senate]]" to ignore these claims.<ref name="Death Star Blog" />

The Galactic Empire Public Relations statement referred to Earth disparagingly as "tiny," "aggressive," and "unimaginatively named." [[Grand Moff/Legends|Grand Moff]] [[Wilhuff Tarkin/Legends|Wilhuff Tarkin]] was quoted as saying that a "primitive" planet like Earth would only have disturbed galactic peace with a Death Star, unlike an "enlightened" leader such as [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Galactic Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]].<ref name="Death Star Blog" />
{{Noncanonend}}

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|The bad news is that I have no idea where we are.|Han Solo|<ref name="Into the Great Unknown">{{Tales|19|Into the Great Unknown}}</ref>}}
The picture of Earth used on [[The Walt Disney Company|Disney's]] website for ''[[Star Tours: The Adventures Continue]]''<ref name="Disneygo" /> is [[Wikipedia:The Blue Marble|''The Blue Marble'']], which was created by [[Wikipedia:NASA|NASA]] and was the most detailed true-color image of the entire Earth as of [[2002]].<ref name="Blue Marble">{{WebCite|url=https://visibleearth.nasa.gov/images/57723/the-blue-marble|text=The Blue Marble|work=NASA Visible Earth|archivedate=20200816141431}}</ref> Although technically taking place in a galaxy far, far away from the Milky Way galaxy, Earth was used in some pre-Disney-acquisition [[Star Wars Legends|Expanded Universe]] sources. One early example was ''[[The Star Wars Intergalactic Passport]]'', which noted it was not a valid passport for use in international travel on Earth.<ref name="IGP" />

The opening crawl shown during the grand opening of ''Star Tours: The Adventures Continue'' at [[Wikipedia:Disney Hollywood Studios|Disney Hollywood Studios]] mentioned the "[[Earth system]]."<ref name="ST:AC">''[[Star Tours: The Adventures Continue]]''</ref> The system's name likewise implied the name of the planet was Earth, which was later confirmed on the ''Star Tours: The Adventures Continue'' destinations section on the official [[Disneyland]] website.<ref>[[Disneyland|''Disneyland'']]</ref>

Prior to the official use of the planet Earth in ''Star Tours: The Adventures Continue'', Earth was also shown in several works considered non-canon within the Legends continuity.

A planet named Urthha featured in ''[[Monsters and Aliens from George Lucas]]''. This book combined photos and concept art from the [[original trilogy]] and other [[Lucasfilm]] productions with a variety of short fiction pieces, and contains two significant references to Earth. In one of them, a [[Wikipedia:Supermarket tabloid|supermarket tabloid]] parody attributed to [[Trebor Uarrac]] of ''[[Galactic Gossip]]'', two [[Duros/Legends|Duros]] newlyweds named [[Etro Edthatt|Etro]] and [[Droza Edthatt]] are "[[Wikipedia:abduction phenomenon|abducted by human beings]]" from the planet "Urthha." A picture of the Edthatts, originally a production photo from [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']], is included with the story. The Duros in the original picture were canonically identified as [[Chachi De Maal/Legends|Chachi De Maal]] and [[Ohwun De Maal/Legends|Ohwun De Maal]].<ref name="Monsters and Aliens from George Lucas">''[[Monsters and Aliens from George Lucas]]''</ref> ''Monsters and Aliens from George Lucas'' is not considered part of ''Star Wars'' Legends, making these two stories non-canonical in that continuity.<ref name="Chee">{{SWBoards|url=thread.jspa?threadID=152583&start=690#14724917|thread=Holocron continuity database questions|user=[[Leland Chee|Leland Y Chee]]|date=2006-05-03|time=5:45 PM|quote=And is information from Monsters and Aliens from George Lucas canon? Unless referred to by a source that is in-continuity, the information is non-continuity.}}</ref> No official source has ever explicitly stated that Urthha and Earth were the same planet.

Another was "[[Into the Great Unknown]]," a comic story which was published as part of [[Star Wars Tales 19|''Star Wars Tales'' 19]]. "Into the Great Unknown" featured Earth, although its name was never directly referenced.<ref name="Into the Great Unknown" /> It acted as a crossover between the ''Star Wars'' and the ''Indiana Jones'' franchises, which were both not only developed by [[George Lucas]] and written by Lucasfilm, but also featured [[Harrison Ford]] in a role (as Han Solo and the titular protagonist, respectively).<ref name="George Lucas: The Creative Impulse">''[[George Lucas: The Creative Impulse]]''</ref> The specific setting on the planet was cited to be the Pacific Northwest,<ref name="Into the Great Unknown" /> which in real life was used as the film setting for Endor in [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']], which was subtly referenced by Han Solo's comment that the forest he crash-landed in resembled [[Endor/Legends|Endor]]. In addition, [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]] being called [[Wikipedia:Sasquatch|Sasquatch]]<ref name="Into the Great Unknown" /> likewise referenced how [[Peter Mayhew]], Chewbacca's actor, had to be accompanied by crew members wearing bright vests while in costume so he would not be mistaken for Sasquatch (also known as Bigfoot) by people who had stumbled upon the filming set. The events of the comic, in addition to referencing ''Star Wars'', also included some references to the ''Indiana Jones'' franchise. Dr. Jones' reference to [[Atlantis]]<ref name="Into the Great Unknown" /> indicated that the comic took place after the events of [[W:c:IndianaJones:Indiana Jones and the Fate of Atlantis|''Indiana Jones and the Fate of Atlantis'']].<ref>{{VisualMediaCite|title=[[Wikipedia:Indiana Jones and the Fate of Atlantis|''Indiana Jones and the Fate of Atlantis'']]|director=[[Hal Barwood]]|prod=[[LucasArts]]|year=[[1992]]}}</ref>

The most recent extensive appearance of Earth was in the [[Star Wars Blog]] post "Planet Earth Abandons Death Star Project In Face Of Galactic Imperial Power." This blog article regarding Earth's decision to abandon plans to create a Death Star was a response to a statement posted from the office of the actual U.S. White House regarding a petition submitted through the U.S. government's "We the People" petition website which had gathered 34,435 signatures. The tongue-in-cheek statement, titled "This Isn't the Petition You're Looking For" (a reference to [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi's]] famous line "These aren't the droids you're looking for" when using the [[Mind trick/Legends|Mind trick]]), estimated a cost of $850,000,000,000,000,000 for the construction of a Death Star and noted that the administration did not support blowing up planets.<ref name="notthepetition">{{WebCite|url=https://petitions.whitehouse.gov/petition/secure-resources-and-funding-and-begin-construction-death-star-2016|text=This Isn't the Petition Response You're Looking For|archivedate=20150813021508}}</ref> At the time, a minimum of at least 25,000 signatures were required, though this requirement was later increased to 100,000, largely in response to such petitions, which were seen as frivolous.<ref name="Guardian">{{WebCite|url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2013/jan/16/white-house-petitions-100000-signatures|text=White House petitions will now require 100,000 signatures before response|author=Holpuch, Amanda|date=2013-01-16|archivedate=20180925115859}}</ref> The Star Wars Blog staff responded to the White House announcement as if it were an [[in-universe]] breaking report from an Imperial standpoint.<ref name="Death Star Blog">{{SW|url=news/planet-earth-abandons-death-star-project-in-face-of-superior-galactic-imperial-power|text=Planet Earth Abandons Death Star Project In Face Of Superior Galactic Imperial Power}}</ref>
